questions.question: A Python function app runs correctly on a developer workstation by using Azure Functions Core Tools. After deployment to Azure, the function fails because an environment variable named MODEL_DEPLOYMENT is not found. The value is defined in local.settings.json. What should you do?

options.text: Add MODEL_DEPLOYMENT as an application setting on the function app
options.why: Correct. local.settings.json is used only by Core Tools locally and is not published. Application settings provide environment variables in Azure.

options.text: Add MODEL_DEPLOYMENT to the extensions section of host.json
options.why: host.json configures the Functions runtime and extensions. It does not define environment variables for code.

options.text: Redeploy by using zip deploy so that local.settings.json is included
options.why: local.settings.json is not intended to be deployed and is not used by the function app in Azure.

options.text: Rename local.settings.json to settings.json
options.why: The Functions host does not read a settings.json file for application settings.

questions.explanation: Values in local.settings.json must be recreated as application settings in Azure, for example by using az functionapp config appsettings set.

questions.scenario: A function uses @app.service_bus_queue_trigger(..., connection="ServiceBusConnection"). The function app has a system-assigned managed identity that has the Azure Service Bus Data Receiver role on the queue. Connection strings must not be used.
questions.question: Which application setting should you add?

options.text: ServiceBusConnection__fullyQualifiedNamespace set to the namespace host name, such as contoso.servicebus.windows.net
options.why: Correct. The __fullyQualifiedNamespace suffix tells the runtime to connect by using the managed identity.

options.text: ServiceBusConnection set to the RootManageSharedAccessKey connection string
options.why: This is a connection string that contains a key, which the requirement prohibits.

options.text: AzureWebJobsServiceBus set to the namespace resource ID
options.why: The trigger looks for settings that start with the connection name ServiceBusConnection, and a resource ID is not a valid value.

options.text: FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME set to servicebus
options.why: FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME identifies the language worker, such as python.

questions.explanation: Identity-based connections use settings that share the connection name as a prefix followed by a double underscore and a property such as fullyQualifiedNamespace.

questions.question: You need to host a new Python function app that scales to zero when idle, integrates with a virtual network, and can avoid cold starts for HTTP functions. Costs must be based on usage where possible. Which hosting option should you choose?

options.text: Flex Consumption plan with always-ready instances for the HTTP functions
options.why: Correct. Flex Consumption scales to zero, supports virtual network integration, and always-ready instances reduce cold starts.

options.text: Consumption plan
options.why: The legacy Consumption plan does not support virtual network integration and has cold starts.

options.text: Dedicated plan on an App Service plan
options.why: A Dedicated plan does not scale to zero and is billed for the plan regardless of usage.

options.text: Premium plan with no minimum instances
options.why: Premium always keeps at least one instance running and does not scale to zero.

questions.explanation: Flex Consumption is the recommended serverless plan for new function apps and supports always-ready instances and virtual network integration.

questions.question: You must change the maximum number of Service Bus messages that each instance of a function app processes concurrently. The change must apply to all Service Bus-triggered functions in the app. Where should you make the change?

options.text: In the extensions.serviceBus section of host.json
options.why: Correct. host.json contains runtime and extension settings that apply to every function in the app.

options.text: In local.settings.json
options.why: local.settings.json applies only when running locally and is not deployed.

options.text: In the queue properties of the Service Bus namespace
options.why: Queue properties such as lock duration are set on the queue, but concurrency per instance is a Functions host setting.

options.text: In the requirements.txt file
options.why: requirements.txt lists Python packages. It does not configure the runtime.

questions.explanation: Settings such as maxConcurrentCalls are configured in host.json, which is deployed with the project.

questions.question: You are deploying a Python function project to a new function app in the Flex Consumption plan by using command-line tools. Which TWO commands should you use?

options.text: az functionapp create with the --flexconsumption-location parameter
options.why: Correct. This creates a function app in the Flex Consumption plan in the specified region.

options.text: func azure functionapp publish followed by the function app name
options.why: Correct. Core Tools packages and deploys the project, with a remote build for Python.

options.text: func start
options.why: func start runs the project locally. It does not deploy it.

options.text: az servicebus queue create
options.why: This creates a Service Bus queue. It does not create or deploy a function app.

questions.explanation: Create the app with az functionapp create --flexconsumption-location, then publish the project with func azure functionapp publish, zip deploy, or a CI/CD pipeline.
